ios.desc:
FocalPaint's unique brush engine simulates thick paint and real pigment mixing with accurate physics models.

Features:
- Realistic color blending behaves like real paint!
- Real canvas texture and paint thickness
- Transparent Ink simulation
- Open Source GPU shader code library for reference and customization
- Write your own custom brush with Metal GPU or Javascript code
- Write your own custom layer modes with Metal GPU code
- Apple Pencil Pro support with hover
- 16 channel "spectral" color model (256 bits per pixel)
- Wide color gamut (P3)

Please note: Apple A12 GPU or newer is required

Terms of Use:
https://www.focalpaint.com/p/terms-of-use.html

Privacy Policy:

quotes.text:
The only applications I'm aware of that currently do spectral rendering on the fly are painting apps.

I have one called Brushwork ( https://brushworkvr.com ) that upsamples RGB from 3 to a larger number of samples spread across visible light, mixes paint in the upsampled space, and then downsamples for rendering (the upsampling approach that app uses is from Scott Burns http://scottburns.us/color-science-projects/ ). FocalPaint on iOS does something similar ( https://apps.apple.com/us/app/focalpaint/id1532688085 ).

I'm happy that tech like this will open up more apps to use spectral rendering.
